<p>Gemini-TTS is the latest evolution of our Cloud TTS
technology that moves beyond natural-sounding speech and provides granular
control over generated audio using text-based prompts. Using
Gemini-TTS, you can synthesize single or multi-speaker speech from
short snippets to long-form narratives, precisely dictating style, accent, pace,
tone, and even emotional expression, all steerable through natural-language
prompts.</p>

<h2 id="additional_controls" data-text="Additional controls" tabindex="-1" role="presentation"><span class="devsite-heading" role="heading" aria-level="2">Additional controls</span><button type="button" class="devsite-heading-link button-flat material-icons" aria-label="Copy link to this section: Additional controls" data-title="Copy link to this section: Additional controls" data-id="additional_controls"></button></h2>

<p>Additional controls and capabilities include the following:</p>

<ol>
<li><p><strong>Natural conversation</strong>: Voice interactions of remarkable quality, more
appropriate expressivity, and patterns of rhythm are delivered with very low
latency so you can converse fluidly.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Style control</strong>: Using natural language prompts, you can adapt the
delivery within the conversation by steering it to adopt specific accents
and produce a range of tones and expressions including a whisper.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Dynamic performance</strong>: These models can bring text to life for expressive
readings of poetry, newscasts, and engaging storytelling. They can also
perform with specific emotions and produce accents when requested.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Enhanced pace and pronunciation control</strong>: Controlling delivery speed
helps to ensure more accuracy in pronunciation including specific words.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>For information on how to choose the right API to use these voices in your application, see <a href="#choose-the-right-api">Choose the right API</a>.</p>

<h2 id="available_regions" data-text="Available regions" tabindex="-1">Available regions</h2>

<p>Gemini-TTS is available multiple regions, through Cloud Text-to-Speech API or Vertex AI API.</p>

<p>The ML processing for these models occurs within the specific region or
multi-region where the request is made. For more information , see
<a href="/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency">Data residency</a>.</p>

<p>For Cloud Text-to-Speech API, the following regions are supported:</p>

<div class="devsite-table-wrapper"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left">Region</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Country or Jurisdiction</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Available models</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">global</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Global (Non-DRZ)</td>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview</code><br><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-flash-tts</code><br><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-pro-tts</code><br><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-tts</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">us</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">United States</td>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-flash-tts</code><br><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-pro-tts</code><br><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-tts</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">eu</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">European Union</td>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-flash-tts</code><br><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-pro-tts</code><br><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-tts</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">northamerica-northeast1</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Canada</td>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-flash-tts</code><br><code translate="no" dir="ltr">gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-tts</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

<p>These regions can be accessed using the following API endpoints:
<code translate="no" dir="ltr"><REGION>-texttospeech.googleapis.com</code>. Note the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">global</code> region doesn't have
a prefix: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">texttospeech.googleapis.com</code>.</p>

<th style="text-align: left">Country or Jurisdiction</th>

</thead>

<tbody>

<h2 id="choose-the-right-api" data-text="Choose the right API" tabindex="-1">Choose the right API</h2>

<p>Discover how to use Gemini-TTS models to synthesize single-speaker and
multi-speaker speech using Cloud Text-to-Speech API or <a href="/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/sdks/overview">Vertex AI API</a>.</p>

<p>Gemini-TTS is available through two APIs to help simplify the integration process for clients. Cloud Text-to-Speech API and Vertex AI API, with REST endpoints and SDKs in multiple programming languages.</p>

<p>Here are some guidelines to help you choose the right API.</p>

<p>If the following applies, choose Cloud Text-to-Speech API:</p>

<ol>
<li>If you are using Chirp 3 HD or other voices, then you can continue to use the same Cloud Text-to-Speech API with minimal incremental updates.</li>
<li>If you need specific output encoding types, Cloud Text-to-Speech API can specify audio encoding. In Vertex AI API, the output is PCM 16bit 24k audio data, and doesn't have WAV headers. If you want to convert to another audio format, then the conversion needs to be handled from the client side.</li>
<li>If you must stream text in multiple chunks, Cloud Text-to-Speech API supports
multiple requests and multiple responses interaction. In contrast,
Vertex AI API supports single request and multiple responses.</li>
<li>If you want to apply <a href="/python/docs/reference/texttospeech/latest/google.cloud.texttospeech_v1.types.AdvancedVoiceOptions">text normalization</a> by default. This is particularly useful for transcripts that include date and monetary values.</li>
</ol>

<p>If the following applies, choose Vertex AI API:</p>

<ol>
<li>If you are already using Gemini-TTS from AI Studio, you can switch to Vertex AI seamlessly to take advantage of the scalability and compliance of Google Cloud.</li>
<li>If you are using Vertex AI API for other models, then the unified api structure makes it easier to start using Gemini-TTS by specifying the model name and voice selection options.</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="use-cloud-text-to-speech-api" data-text="Use Cloud Text-to-Speech API" tabindex="-1">Use Cloud Text-to-Speech API</h2>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> The size of the text field and the prompt field individually can be
at most 4,000 bytes. While the total size of the prompt and text fields can be
up to 8,000 bytes, each field must be a maximum of 4000 bytes. The output audio
can at most be around 655 seconds. If the input text amounts to audio longer
than this limit, the audio will be truncated.</span></aside>
<p>Optionally specify audio formats and sampling rates in "audioConfig" field if non-default options are needed.</p>

<th style="text-align: left">Description</th>

</tr>

<td style="text-align: left">Input</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left">Prompt field</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Less than or equal to 4,000 bytes.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Input</td>
</tr>

<td style="text-align: left">Text and prompt fields</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Less than or equal to 8,000 bytes.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Input</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left">Duration for the output audio</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Approximately 655 seconds. If the input text results in the audio exceeding 655 seconds, the audio is truncated.</td>

<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> To be able to use Gemini-TTS, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">aiplatform.endpoints.predict</code> permission is
required for the model endpoint. This permission can be granted with the
<a href="/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control#aiplatform.user">roles/aiplatform.user role</a>.</span></aside>
<h3 id="before_you_begin" data-text="Before you begin" tabindex="-1">Before you begin</h3>

<p>Before you can begin using Cloud Text-to-Speech, you must enable the API in the
Google Cloud console by following steps:</p>

<ol>
<li>Enable Cloud Text-to-Speech on a project.</li>
<li>Make sure billing is enabled for Cloud Text-to-Speech.</li>
<li>Set up authentication for your development environment.</li>
<li>Assign <code translate="no" dir="ltr">aiplatform.endpoints.predict</code> permission for the authenticated user.
This permission can be granted with the
<a href="/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control#aiplatform.user">roles/aiplatform.user role</a>.</li>
<li>Select the correct API endpoint based on <a href="#available_regions">Available regions</a>.</li>
</ol>

<h4 id="set_up_your_google_cloud_platform_project" data-text="Set up your Google Cloud project" tabindex="-1">Set up your Google Cloud project</h4>

<ol>
<li><p><a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/" target="console" track-type="tasks" track-name="console Link" track-metadata-position="body" class="button button-primary">Sign in to Google Cloud console</a> </p></li>
<li><p><a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/projectselector2/home/dashboard" target="console" track-type="commonIncludes" track-name="consoleLink" track-metadata-end-goal="createProject" class="button button-primary">Go to the project selector page</a></p>

<p>You can either choose an existing project or create a new one. For more
details about creating a project, see the
<a href="/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-projects" target="_blank">Google Cloud documentation</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>If you create a new project, a message appears informing you to link a billing account. If you are using a pre-existing project, make sure to enable billing</p>

<p><a href="/billing/docs/how-to/modify-project" target="_blank" track-type="commonIncludes" track-name="supportLink" track-metadata-end-goal="enableBilling" class="button button-primary">Learn how to confirm that billing is enabled for your project</a></p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> You must enable billing to use Cloud Text-to-Speech API, however, you won't be
be charged unless you exceed the free quota. For more information about pricing, see the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/text-to-speech/pricing">pricing</a> page.</span></aside></li>
<li><p>After you've selected a project and linked it to a billing account, you
can enable the Cloud Text-to-Speech API. Go to the <strong>Search products and
resources</strong> bar at the top of the page, and type in <strong>"speech"</strong>. Select the
<strong>Cloud Text-to-Speech API</strong> from the list of results.</p></li>
<li><p>To try Cloud Text-to-Speech without linking it to your project, choose
the <strong>Try this API</strong> option. To enable the Cloud Text-to-Speech API for use
with your project, click <strong>Enable</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Set up authentication for your development environment. For instructions, see
<a href="/text-to-speech/docs/authentication#authn-how-to">Set up authentication for Cloud Text-to-Speech</a>.</p></li>
</ol>

<h3 id="perform_streaming_single-speaker_synthesis" data-text="Perform streaming single-speaker synthesis" tabindex="-1">Perform streaming single-speaker synthesis</h3>

<p>Streaming synthesis is suitable for real-time applications where fast response
is critical for the user experience. In streaming connection, the API
returns audio as it becomes available in small chunks.</p>

<p>As the caller of the API, make sure to consume the audio chunks, passing them down
to your clients as they arrive (for example, using socketio for web apps).</p>

<p>Cloud Text-to-Speech API supports <code translate="no" dir="ltr">multiple request multiple response</code> type
streaming. While it's possible to send the input chunks to the API
asynchronously as shown in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">request_generator</code>, the API only starts
synthesizing when the client sends <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Half-Close</code> as a signal that it won't send
any more data to the API.</p>

<p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">prompt</code> field must be set in the first input chunk, because it's ignored in
consecutive chunks.</p>

<h3 id="perform_synchronous_multi-speaker_synthesis_with_structured_text_input" data-text="Perform synchronous multi-speaker synthesis with structured text input" tabindex="-1">Perform synchronous multi-speaker synthesis with structured text input</h3>

<p>Multi-speaker with structured text input enables intelligent verbalization of
text in a human-like way. For example, this kind of input is useful for
addresses and dates. Freeform text input speaks the text exactly as written.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> Speaker aliases must consist solely of alphanumeric characters, excluding
whitespace. The combined size of all lines of dialogue can be at most 4,000
bytes. While the total size of the prompt and dialogue can be up to 4,000 bytes,
each prompt and dialogue field must be a maximum of 4,000 bytes.</span></aside>

<h2 id="use-vertex-ai-api" data-text="Use Vertex AI API" tabindex="-1">Use Vertex AI API</h2>

<p>Discover how to use Gemini-TTS models to synthesize single-speaker and
multi-speaker speech using Vertex AI API.</p>

<p>In Cloud Text-to-Speech API, the user can provide text and prompt fields separately. In Vertex AI API, this is a single <code translate="no" dir="ltr">contents</code> field, where it specifies the input in the form of "{prompt}: {text}", eg. "Say the following in a curious way: OK, so... tell me about this AI thing."</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> The total size of the prompt and text fields can be up to 8,000 bytes.
The output audio can at most be around 655 seconds. If the input text amounts to
audio longer than this limit, the audio is truncated.</span></aside>
<div class="devsite-table-wrapper"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left">Description</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Limit</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Type</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left">Contents field</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Less than or equal to 8,000 bytes.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Input</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left">Duration for the output audio</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Approximately 655 seconds. If the input text results in the audio exceeding 655 seconds, the audio is truncated.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Output</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

<h3 id="before_you_begin_2" data-text="Before you begin" tabindex="-1">Before you begin</h3>

<p>Before you can begin, follow the installation steps for
<a href="/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/sdks/overview">Vertex AI API</a>. To take
advantage of data residency options, make sure to set the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">LOCATION</code> based on
<a href="#available_regions">Available regions</a>.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> The API ignores the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">temperature</code>, <code translate="no" dir="ltr">top_k</code> and <code translate="no" dir="ltr">top_p</code> generation config
parameters in the request. </span></aside>

<h2 id="perform_speech_synthesis_in_media_studio" data-text="Perform speech synthesis in Media Studio" tabindex="-1">Perform speech synthesis in Media Studio</h2>



<devsite-expandable is-upgraded="" id="expandable-1">
<a class="exw-control expand-control" track-metadata-position="body" track-metadata-end-goal="viewPermissionsHowToGuides" track-type="task" track-name="iamPermissionsExpandable" aria-controls="expandable-1" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0" role="button"><h4 class="showalways" id="permissions-required-for-this-task" data-text="Permissions required for this task" tabindex="-1">Permissions required for this task</h4></a>

<p>To perform this task, you must have the following
  <a href="/iam/docs/overview#permissions">permissions</a>:



</p><ul>
  <li><code translate="no" dir="ltr">serviceusage.services.use</code></li>
</ul>



</devsite-expandable>

<p>You can use the Media Studio in the Google Google Cloud console to experiment with text-to-speech models. This provides a user interface for quickly generating, listening to synthesized audio and experimenting with different style instructions and parameters.</p>

<ol>
<li><p>In the Google Google Cloud console, go to the <strong>Vertex AI Studio <span aria-label="and then">></span> Media
Studio</strong> page.</p>

<p><a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/studio/media/generate;tab=audio" class="button button-primary" target="console" track-name="consoleLink" track-type="task" track-metadata-position="body">
    Media Studio</a></p></li>
<li><p>Select <strong>Speech</strong> from the media drop-down.</p></li>
<li><p>In the text field, enter the text you want to synthesize into speech.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Settings</strong> pane, configure the following settings:</p>

<ol>
<li><strong>Model</strong>: Select the Cloud TTS (TTS) model that you want to use, such as <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Gemini 2.5 Pro TTS</code>. For more information about available models, see <a href="/text-to-speech/docs/list-voices-and-types">Cloud TTS models</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Style instructions</strong>: Optional: Enter a text prompt that describes the selected speaking style, tone, and emotional delivery. This lets you to guide the model's performance beyond the default narration. For example: <em>"Narrate in a calm, professional tone for a documentary."</em>.</li>
<li><strong>Language</strong>: Select the language and region of the input text. The model generates speech in the selected language and accent. For example, <em>English (United States)</em>.</li>
<li><strong>Voice</strong>: Choose a predefined voice for the narration. The list contains the available voices for the selected model and language, such as <em>Acherner (Female)</em>.</li>
</ol></li>
<li><p>Optional: Expand the Advanced options section to configure technical audio settings:</p>

<ol>
<li><strong>Audio encoding</strong>: Select the encoding for the output audio file. <code translate="no" dir="ltr">LINEAR16</code> is a lossless, uncompressed format suitable for high-quality audio processing. <code translate="no" dir="ltr">MULAW</code> is also available for compressed audio output.</li>
<li><strong>Audio sample rate</strong>: Select the sample rate in hertz (Hz). This determines the audio quality. Higher values like 44,100 Hz represent higher fidelity audio, equivalent to CD quality.</li>
<li><strong>Speed</strong>: Adjust the speaking rate by moving the slider or entering a value. Values less than 1 slow down the speech, and values greater than 1 speed it up. The default is 1.</li>
<li><strong>Volume gain (db)</strong>: Adjust the volume of the output audio in decibels (dB). Positive values increase the volume, and negative values decrease it. The default is 0.</li>
</ol></li>
<li><p>Click the <strong>send</strong> icon at the right of the text-box to generate the audio.</p></li>
<li><p>The generated audio appears in the media player. Click the play button to listen to the output. You can continue to adjust the settings, and generate new versions as needed.</p></li>
</ol>

<h2 id="prompting_tips" data-text="Prompting tips" tabindex="-1">Prompting tips</h2>

<p>Creating engaging and natural-sounding audio from text requires understanding the nuances of spoken language and translating them into script form. The following tips will help you craft scripts that sound authentic and capture the chosen tone.</p>

<h3 id="the_three_levers_of_speech_control" data-text="The three levers of speech control" tabindex="-1">The three levers of speech control</h3>

<p>For the most predictable and nuanced results, ensure all three of the following components are consistent with your desired output.</p>

<p><strong>Style Prompt</strong>
The primary driver of the overall emotional tone and delivery. The prompt sets the context for the entire speech segment.</p>

<ul>
<li><p>Example: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">You are an AI assistant speaking in a friendly and helpful tone.</code></p></li>
<li><p>Example: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Narrate this in the calm, authoritative tone of a nature documentary narrator.</code></p></li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Text Content</strong>
The semantic meaning of the words you are synthesizing. An evocative phrase that is emotionally consistent with the style prompt will produce much more reliable results than neutral text.</p>

<ul>
<li><p>Good: A prompt for a scared tone works best with text like <code translate="no" dir="ltr">I think someone is in the house.</code></p></li>
<li><p>Less Effective: A prompt for a scared tone with text like <code translate="no" dir="ltr">The meeting is at 4 PM.</code> will produce ambiguous results.</p></li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Markup Tags (Preview)</strong>
Bracketed tags like <code translate="no" dir="ltr">[sigh]</code> are best used for injecting a specific, localized action or style modification, not for setting the overall tone. They work in concert with the style prompt and text content.</p>

<h3 id="markup_tag_guide" data-text="Markup tag guide" tabindex="-1">Markup tag guide</h3>

<p>Our research shows that bracketed markup tags operate in one of three distinct modes. Understanding a tag's mode is key to using it effectively.</p>

<h4 id="mode_1_non-speech_sounds" data-text="Mode 1: Non-speech sounds" tabindex="-1">Mode 1: Non-speech sounds</h4>

<p>The markup is replaced by an audible, non-speech vocalization (e.g., a sigh, a laugh). The tag itself is not spoken. These are excellent for adding realistic, human-like hesitations and reactions.</p>

<div class="devsite-table-wrapper"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left">Tag</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Behavior</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Reliability</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Guidance</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[sigh]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Inserts a sigh sound.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">The emotional quality of the sigh is influenced by the prompt.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[laughing]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Inserts a laugh.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">For best results, use a specific prompt. e.g., a generic prompt may yield a laugh of shock, while "react with an amused laugh" creates a laugh of amusement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[uhm]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Inserts a hesitation sound.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Useful for creating a more natural, conversational feel.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

<h4 id="mode_2_style_modifiers" data-text="Mode 2: Style modifiers" tabindex="-1">Mode 2: Style modifiers</h4>

<p>The markup is not spoken, but it modifies the delivery of the subsequent speech. The scope and duration of the modification can vary.</p>

<div class="devsite-table-wrapper"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left">Tag</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Behavior</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Reliability</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Guidance</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[sarcasm]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Imparts a sarcastic tone on the subsequent phrase.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">This tag is a powerful modifier. It demonstrates that abstract concepts can successfully steer the model's delivery.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[robotic]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Makes the subsequent speech sound robotic.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">The effect can extend across an entire phrase. A supportive style prompt (e.g., "Say this in a robotic way") is still recommended for best results.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[shouting]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Increases the volume of the subsequent speech.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Most effective when paired with a matching style prompt (e.g., "Shout this next part") and text that implies yelling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[whispering]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Decreases the volume of the subsequent speech.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Best results are achieved when the style prompt is also explicit (e.g., "now whisper this part as quietly as you can").</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[extremely fast]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Increases the speed of the subsequent speech.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Ideal for disclaimers or fast-paced dialogue. Minimal prompt support needed.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

<h4 id="mode_3_vocalized_markup_adjectives" data-text="Mode 3: Vocalized markup (adjectives)" tabindex="-1">Mode 3: Vocalized markup (adjectives)</h4>

<p>The markup tag itself is spoken as a word, while also influencing the tone of the entire sentence. This behavior typically applies to emotional adjectives.</p>

<p><em>Warning</em>: Because the tag itself is spoken, this mode is likely an undesired side effect for most use cases. Prefer using the Style Prompt to set these emotional tones instead.</p>

<div class="devsite-table-wrapper"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left">Tag</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Behavior</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Reliability</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Guidance</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[scared]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">The word "scared" is spoken, and the sentence adopts a scared tone.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Performance is highly dependent on text content. The phrase "I just heard a window break" produces a genuinely scared result. A neutral phrase produces a "spooky" but less authentic result.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[curious]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">The word "curious" is spoken, and the sentence adopts a curious tone.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Use an inquisitive phrase to support the tag's intent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[bored]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">The word "bored" is spoken, and the sentence adopts a bored, monotone delivery.</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Use with text that is mundane or repetitive for best effect.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

<h4 id="mode_4_pacing_and_pauses" data-text="Mode 4: Pacing and pauses" tabindex="-1">Mode 4: Pacing and pauses</h4>

<p>These tags insert silence into the generated audio, giving you granular control over rhythm, timing, and pacing. Standard punctuation (commas, periods, semicolons) will also create natural pauses, but these tags offer more explicit control.</p>

<div class="devsite-table-wrapper"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left">Tag</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Behavior</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Reliability</th>
<th style="text-align: left">Guidance</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[short pause]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Inserts a brief pause, similar to a comma (~250ms).</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Use to separate clauses or list items for better clarity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[medium pause]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Inserts a standard pause, similar to a sentence break (~500ms).</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Effective for separating distinct sentences or thoughts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">[long pause]</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left">Inserts a significant pause for dramatic effect (~1000ms+).</td>
<td style="text-align: left">High</td>
<td style="text-align: left">Use for dramatic timing. For example: "The answer is... <code translate="no" dir="ltr">[long pause]</code> ...no." Avoid overuse, as it can sound unnatural.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div>

<h4 id="key_strategies_for_reliable_results" data-text="Key strategies for reliable results" tabindex="-1">Key strategies for reliable results</h4>

<ul>
<li><p><strong>Align all three levers:</strong>
For maximum predictability, ensure your Style Prompt, Text Content, and any Markup Tags are all semantically consistent and working toward the same goal.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Use emotionally rich text:</strong>
Don't rely on prompts and tags alone. Give the model rich, descriptive text to work with. This is especially critical for nuanced emotions like sarcasm, fear, or excitement.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Write specific, detailed prompts:</strong>
The more specific your style prompt, the more reliable the result. "React with an amused laugh" is better than just <code translate="no" dir="ltr">[laughing]</code>. "Speak like a 1940s radio news announcer" is better than "Speak in an old-fashioned way."</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Test and verify new tags:</strong>
The behavior of a new or untested tag is not always predictable. A tag you assume is a style modifier might be vocalized. Always test a new tag or prompt combination to confirm its behavior before deploying to production.</p></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="safety_check_settings" data-text="Safety check settings" tabindex="-1">Safety check settings</h2>

<p>While some safety checks cannot be disabled, you can adjust the thresholds for certain harm categories to further enhance safety and minimize misuse. This can be optionally enabled by setting safety filters under <a href="/python/docs/reference/texttospeech/latest/google.cloud.texttospeech_v1.types.AdvancedVoiceOptions">AdvancedVoiceOptions</a>.</p>

<p>There are <a href="/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/multimodal/configure-safety-filters#harm_categories">4 harm categories</a> that can be configured at different levels of threshold. One or more categories can be set to block harmful content.</p>

<p>The legacy <code translate="no" dir="ltr">relax_safety_filters</code> field is deprecated.</p>

<p>Depending on the safety filters that you configure, your output may contain a
safety code similar to: "Cloud Text-to-Speech could not generate audio because the input text or prompt
violates Vertex AI's usage guidelines. If you think this was an error, send
feedback. Support codes: <b>62263041</b>"</p>

<p>The code listed in the output corresponds to a specific harmful category.</p>
